A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUS/UOT research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original English DWUG experiments on instance-level change, word-level change magnitude, and semantic scope, with numerical comparisons and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds Spanish word-level experiments and English stable-versus-changed word analyses.

M1.justification: The UOT objective, SUS definitions, embedding model, and word-level aggregation methods remain unchanged, including the alternative metrics already in v1 Appendix G. Expanded LDR documentation and an alternative-weighting check do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only English DWUG. v2 Appendix H adds Spanish DWUG evaluations for both word-level change magnitude and semantic scope, substantially extending language coverage. Instance-level evaluation remains English-only.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds WiDiD to the sense-level comparison previously reported for SUS and LDR in v1 Section 6. The word-level comparator sets remain unchanged, including when extended to Spanish.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds separate test evaluations for stable and changed words while retaining pooled validation tuning. Section 5.1 also reports testing embedding-norm weights. The original English 8:2 validation/test design and tuning grids remain unchanged; Spanish experiments reuse the existing protocol.

E4.justification: New Tables 9–10 analyze instance-level and sense-level performance separately for 25 stable and 21 changed words. Section 5.1 adds a brief weighting ablation reporting little effect from embedding-norm weights. Existing hyperparameter sensitivity analyses and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already document 100 random validation/test splits and report average test performance in Appendix C. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds Spanish results and English subgroup results. Spanish Table 13 reports 0.61 for fSUS, fOT, and fAPD; Table 14 reports 0.45 for g1 versus 0.41 for gvMF. English sense-level SUS/LDR correlations change from 0.85/0.74 to 0.83/0.70, with WiDiD newly reported at 0.84. Existing English word-level scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The OT/UOT formulations, SUS definitions, aggregation mathematics, and convexity discussion are retained. Expanded vMF and LDR formulas explain the existing baseline computation rather than introducing a new theoretical argument, proof, or substantive assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: using UOT alignment discrepancies to quantify instance-level semantic change and aggregate it into word-level magnitude and broadening/narrowing measures.

C2.justification: v2 explains poor stable-word correlations through sensitivity of rankings to small fluctuations, notes that sense-derived gold scores favor WiDiD, and interprets Spanish results as additional support. It also explains the limited effect of norm-based weights. The English-only limitation is retained despite the Spanish experiments.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix B now explicitly document embedding normalization, vMF mean-direction estimation, and the concentration-parameter approximation used for LDR. Appendix H states that Spanish experiments reuse the existing protocol and tuning range. Code and data access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Banerjee et al. (2005) for vMF estimation and Zamora-Reina et al. (2022) for the Spanish benchmark. The central positioning relative to OT, sense-based methods, and prior instance-level research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the LDR explanation in Section 4.4 and Appendix B, revises the results discussion in Appendix F, and adds Appendix H. There are localized language, affiliation, and acknowledgment edits, while the main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a sense-level column, and four compact result tables are added. The existing gold-sense plot moves from v1 Figure 8 into v2 Figure 5, while Figure 3 becomes a larger vertically stacked display. These are localized changes within the retained layout and visual style.

improvement.justification: Spanish word-level validation broadens the empirical support, subgroup analyses expose weaker performance on stable words, and fuller LDR documentation improves reproducibility. These provide a useful but limited overall improvement: cross-language evidence does not cover the central instance-level task, and the unchanged English-only limitation creates an internal inconsistency.
